I've been working this land for 25 years and I know what it can do. My wheat-maize rotation is the backbone — it fills the grain account and keeps the soil from going lazy. Stevia pays better per mu when the buyers come, so I keep a piece of land in it, but not so much that I'm overwhelmed when the family is away working in town.

My 90 mu: I put 60 mu into the wheat-maize rotation — same ground, two crops a year. The other 30 mu goes to stevia. That's been my split for a few years now and it works.

For winter wheat, I'll use the improved seed I get from the county supply station — not the most expensive, but it's what my neighbors use and it yields well. I do three irrigations: one before freeze-up, one at jointing, one at heading. Rotary tillage after maize harvest, then I sow. I keep nitrogen at 15 kg per mu, same as last year. Yield should be around 480 kg.

For summer maize, I drill hybrid seed straight into the stubble — no plowing, saves fuel and the soil holds moisture better. Rain is usually decent in July-August so I only plan two waterings. Nitrogen higher here, 18 kg, split into base and topdress at V6. I aim for 550 kg per mu.

Stevia I plant cuttings in spring. It needs more water than grain crops and the potassium must be right or the leaves go thin. I do five irrigations and watch for aphids — two pesticide runs are usually enough. I harvest three cuttings through the season. Dried leaf should come to about 200 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.
